nodes.claim: Center built from intersection of completed lower-level movements
Continuous valid trading is a precondition, sudden suspension/voiding is outside assumed domain
Recover principal and manage remaining shares, distinct from zero mark-to-market exposure
Current signals determine actions; future B or c is not guaranteed
Multiple legitimate descriptions possible due to level/time resolution and center extensions
Trade-level base case proposed to break center/movement circular dependence
Movement connection is associative but not commutative
T+1 fees and errors limit operational timeframe
Associative regrouping admits multiple time/level interpretations and different third-buy boundaries
Trend divergence requires same-level centers A and B plus extremum continuation constraints
Uniqueness is claimed under a fixed same-level decomposition rule, not all alternative rule choices
Later editorial note flags missing Ai/Ai+2 non-new-high/low condition
Multi-level allocations imply stock/cash conservation in a unified brokerage account
Small-level contrarian buy/sell signals may be overrun by non-exhausted higher-level trend
Post-close review of trades and psychological decision process; not a medical diagnosis
Divergence level may equal or be smaller than current movement level and higher-level outcome is not predetermined
Final lower-level center third-class sell/buy signal is necessary, not sufficient, for small divergence leading to larger reversal
Hold stock or cash while observing unfinished movement; AI implementation adds tradeability and deadline constraints
Eight completed half-hour bars define full-day auxiliary central-overlap classification; interim labels cannot use future bars
Intraday 2007 example includes author-claimed exact points and explicitly recognizes T+1 next-day exit risk
Author repeats zero-cost-is-no-risk claim; remaining stock price risk persists under economic mark-to-market
Author claims two profit-maximizing operational modes under a fixed level but needs explicit feasible set and objective
Market structure/segments should be identified before selecting the auxiliary MACD sampling period
Public stock recommendations may affect follower demand and cannot automatically establish independent prediction skill
Observing, predicting, and participating traders jointly shape observed market; structural scale invariance is an unverified author's claim
Three types of buy/sell points have distinct functions at one operating level despite smaller-scale interrelations
A separately dated 2009-01-05 discussion on third-class buy/sell points begins mid-page 162 and extends over pages 163–164
Multiple associatively regrouped descriptions remain constrained by mandatory lower-level connector between two same-level centers
Long accumulation and exit can have different time strategies, but must obey actual cash/share accounting
Overnight 5·30 shock can render an earlier ideal first sell unexecutable; later second or third sell requires current confirmation
Micro-retracement detection threshold may vary, but comparable cases must use one fixed segmentation policy
A possible divergence leg can be invalidated by later acceleration, so prediction cannot be marked confirmed
Author's 3994.57 versus 3994.21 comparison depends on prior precision; truncation and half-up integer rounding disagree
Unexpected news is assessed by the level of structural disruption but does not remove portfolio price or gap risk
Vol3 lesson61 header is dated 2010-08-13 yet internal source contains distinct 2007-06-22/27 dated commentary
Three-K-line fractals and pen/segment structure are built from cleaned non-containing bars with minimum interval requirements
The phrase 新笔定义 appears following the original explanation; provenance and revised rule must be versioned separately
Data bar sampling frequency is not automatically equal to the level of the observed recursive center or movement
A price comparison tolerance and integer policy must remain fixed; proximity is not transitive
K-line containment is not transitive; the operator must merge successive bars in order and track original sources
No price-only evidence can identify a single omnipotent operator; multiple capital interests may interact
Opposite-direction strokes form a segment feature sequence; adjacent nonoverlap is a feature gap
First-second feature gap requires later opposite-sequence fractal before locally confirming segment termination
Partition observable price states by prior boundary and respond on actual triggered condition, not fixed future price prediction
Provisional monthly fractal/pen may be revised before completion; confirmed structure cannot be retroactively backdated
After an existing center forms, third buy, third sell, or extension/expansion are different possible outcomes requiring observed confirmation
Only strict elements of the same feature sequence may be containment-merged; tentative transition-side features may be auxiliary or unknown
Morphology vs dynamics and chapter 64 informal segment claims were later tightened by chapter 67 feature-sequence definitions
Center up-movement and center oscillation are author's structural opportunity types; they do not ensure actual after-cost positive profits
Author calls policy risk nonsystematic while later editorial note challenges this as broad systematic risk
Self-described dream-like market opponent stories are unattributed narrative claims rather than independently verified trading events
Author's self-described dream market-opponent stories cannot prove counterpart identity or manipulation
Unique pen decomposition presupposes formal completed fractals, non-overlapping K-line definitions and handling of equal extrema
A line segment may be normalized into a high-low derived view for higher level center analysis without changing its original path or confirmation time
Earlier intraday lower-level signal does not imply that the third daily fractal bar has already closed and confirmed
Strong sell discipline and completed technical conditions cannot guarantee realized gain or eliminate repurchase opportunity cost
Different dated original source corrects previous figures and proposes revised pen conditions, requiring independent version and dataset provenance
Confirmed 3-bar fractal still needs later evidence to decide continuation versus extension to a pen; trading psych interpretation is not observed actor intent
Original author prefers segments as minimum center building blocks for claimed noise robustness, an independent testable hypothesis
Author replaces term self-similarity with self-isomorphic structure and separates f1 base extraction from f2 higher-level recursion
Author's unverified past-market story and self-assessed legal status cannot prove actual behavior or regulatory judgment
Interpretation of a lower-level third sell varies by a known higher-level center rising/falling/oscillating context; later editorial cases are source separated
First-person dream-like market behavior and zero-accounting-cost claims do not verify trading actor identity or risk-free economic value
Old movement termination may precede confirmed new movement, requiring an unresolved middle period with prior center as read-only context
Center component and completed consolidation movement type are distinct; necessary structural existence is not a trading-profit guarantee
BOLL band width squeeze is auxiliary timing heuristic, cannot itself confirm movement termination or third buy/sell points
Author models two-valued pen direction and phase as a canonical four-state finite-transition system, not independently established unique OHLC identification
Center A/B midpoint Z and suboscillation midpoint Zn monitor strength; Zn outside center boundaries does not suffice for confirmed third buy/sell
Same (1,0) fractal candidate can lead to continuation or reversal; conservative and oscillation-skilled decisions are distinct optional policies
Conditional future price-structure opportunities need trade execution proof, including same-day sale restrictions for newly purchased T+1 A-shares
Recovered initial external cash or self-reported zero contribution does not remove remaining marked-to-market financial exposure
Author criticizes gambling anchors, fear of missing out, chasing and uncontrolled capital additions; no empirical proof of guaranteed profitability
Author's medical/strategy analogies distinguish theoretical classification, observation and actionable implementation with different evidence requirements
Author advocates conditional post-divergence plans without guessing which future branch will happen and notes T+1 execution limits
Author invokes associative resegmentation to retain valid centers across undefined middle period, requiring distinct as-of and hindsight views
Author two-way fifth-minute third-sell branches coexist with later editorial claim that actual trajectory fell outside the original two-way account
Author allows second buy price lower than first buy; structurally completed second buy and independent third-buy overlap must be separated
Author likens recursive market-movement unique decomposition to positional number bases, but full formal uniqueness requires a specified parser and proofs
Author proposes zero-axis MACD DIF/DEA defensive heuristic using preselected minimum chart timeframe, not empirically demonstrated no-loss
Author proposes link between market geometries and energy dynamics, with prominent 2010 editorial additions that do not prove physical law or historical profitability
Author favors mechanical fractal/pen operation; rule expressibility is separate from timely observable signal, legal fill, and realized net profit
MA rebound nine-level ordinal classification and sector mean require complete as-of inputs, frozen rules and constituent snapshots
30-minute rebound discussed using sublevel 5-minute up-down-up elements; third segment high is not guaranteed higher; actual fills separate
Fractal boundary and first-buy-center-third-buy/sell are distinct bottom definitions, neither a completed forward signal without later evidence
